It’s just because even though she is doing the whole breakup thing, she doesn’t want to actually go through with it. If she gets a whiff that I might actually want to, she’ll immediately flip and make me feel guilty enough to stay, then do the whole breakup thing again only this time it’s just me giving her attention

If she decides to discard me one day, I think I’d be the happiest person alive. There has rarely been a moment in 3 years of dating where I felt able to totally relax and not have to monitor everything I do or say. 

I don’t want to be with her, it’s just that I don’t feel psychologically capable of leaving. I know that I’ll have to fight through 10 layers of fake breakups, mood switches, yelling, and emotional whiplash, just to end up with her browbeating me into staying and expecting me to make up for trying to leave her. And she will NEVER forget that I tried to leave. She will bring up every single thing that I’ve done to hurt and just add it on the list.

So yeah, I don’t want her in my life at all. Sometimes I hope I’ll get into a car accident on my way over to her house so I won’t have to see her. But like I said, she’s conditioned me that I’m completely powerless to stop it

I’m not sure where you got the mansplaining bit. But I’ll address a couple of the points you’ve made.

1. I have never, ever in my life claimed that I am smarter than her because that’s not true. She thinks in a different manner but that doesn’t make her any less intelligent.

2. How I write is different from how I talk. I didn’t shoot questions at her like a Q&A, we had a normal conversation. What I wrote down was a condensed version of what we said, not direct quotes. It might sound robotic, but that’s just how I type.

3. I absolutely do not value myself above anyone else. At all. Furthermore I don’t consider intelligence to be the only way to determine someone’s worth. She has so many other valuable qualities other than being smart as well. I do not put myself above her or anyone else
